name: Combined Oxidative Phosphorylation Defect Type 23
aliases: Combined Mitochondrial Oxidative Phosphorylation Deficiency Type 23

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Combined Oxidative Phosphorylation Defect Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Early onset multisystemic symptoms including neurological and muscular involvement
Deficient activity of multiple respiratory chain complexes in muscle or fibroblasts
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with oxidative phosphorylation machinery
Brain MRI showing basal ganglia and brainstem abnormalities
Elevated blood or CSF lactate levels indicating mitochondrial dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: clinical presentation, biochemical evidence, and genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other mitochondrial and metabolic disorders.

occasional.symptomName: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex IV
Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex I
Abnormal basal ganglia MRI signal intensity

laboratory: Elevated blood and CSF lactate and pyruvate levels
Combined deficiency of mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes I, III, and IV in muscle biopsy
Elevated serum creatine kinase in some cases
imaging: Brain MRI showing basal ganglia lesions, cerebral atrophy, and brainstem abnormalities
Cardiac echocardiogram demonstrating hypertrophic or dilated cardiomyopathy
genetic: Pathogenic variants in nuclear genes encoding mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation components or assembly factors
Mitochondrial DNA depletion or multiple deletions may be present
other: Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers and abnormal mitochondrial morphology on electron microscopy

distinguishingFeatures: Isolated complex I deficiency rather than combined complex deficiencies
More variable age of onset and clinical presentation
Characteristic symmetrical lesions in basal ganglia and brainstem on MRI
Often associated with specific mitochondrial or nuclear gene mutations distinct from COXPD23

redFlags: Rapidly progressive neurological deterioration in infancy
Severe lactic acidosis refractory to treatment
Multisystem involvement including cardiomyopathy and liver dysfunction
references: Rahman S, et al. Mitochondrial disease: clinical features and diagnosis. J Inherit Metab Dis. 2020.
